title: The Soldier Who Kept Fighting WWII Until 1974
notes: Public-domain photographs of Onoda exist on Commons and are used. The 1944 photograph with his brother Shigeo (p04) is used twice deliberately.

The 1944 images are tagged public domain on Commons under Japanese law for photographs of that period. That status is well established but is a determination by Commons editors, not a statement from the rights holder; it is worth knowing if a claim is ever made.

Segments s25 to s27 concern the roughly thirty Filipino islanders killed by Onoda's group. The frame is held still and empty on purpose: no cast, no props, no graphics. Do not substitute anything more dramatic.
No illustrated violence anywhere: no shooting, no victims, no firefights. Deaths are carried by stillness and empty places.
Every archival URL was resolved from the Commons API and checked live.
LOW RESOLUTION: surrender 1974 (37KB), Kozuka (55KB), Hiroo and Shigeo 1944 (78KB), Onoda young (104KB). Show them as cards at native size, never upscaled.
Guide objects: Onoda's rifle (the bolt opens and closes the story) and Taniguchi's folded order.

onoda.desc: Hiroo Onoda as a lean Japanese soldier in a patched, faded 1940s uniform and field cap, rifle slung, simple vague face, no likeness; also a young civilian version in a 1940s suit

taniguchi.desc: Major Yoshimi Taniguchi: in 1944 an officer in uniform; in 1974 a man in his sixties in a cardigan, later in his old uniform again, simple vague face

suzuki.desc: Norio Suzuki, a 24-year-old Japanese traveller in 1970s jeans and a big backpack, simple vague face

comrades.desc: three Japanese soldiers in patched uniforms, Akatsu, Shimada and Kozuka, simple vague faces, drawn as a group that can be reduced one at a time

crowd.desc: a lineup of extras: search party in 1950s gear, 1974 press photographers, airport crowd, Brazilian ranch hands, Japanese schoolchildren with backpacks, simple vague faces
